_about: The chat's commands that read or change the agent file (2026-09-26, interactive-mode spec section 3): the same words and behaviour in both SDKs.
words: every sentence as a template, equal to TypeScript cli/chat-words.ts CHAT_WORDS and Python cli/repl/chat_words.py CHAT_WORDS.
loader: the sentences the agent-file loaders say (both SDKs, spec 3.1), and cases run through parseAgentMarkdown / AgentFile.
cases: run through handleInput / handle_input with the prompts mocked. files are made in a fresh folder the chat starts in ({"link": target} makes a symbolic link);
agent picks the agent by name (robutler for the built-in one; unset finds it the usual way); env sets variables; model is -m; cwd 'home' starts the chat in HOME;
then_write and then_link change files after the chat loaded; editor names a script the test makes (append adds a line to $1, fail exits 3) and sets EDITOR to it, none unsets it;
interactive is the terminal seam; typed lines run in order; answers are what the person types at each question, asked are the questions, in order;

printed lines must each appear, in order, in what the chat printed (compared with runs of whitespace collapsed, so wrapping does not matter); {folder} is the chat's folder and {known} the loader's key list;
files_after are exact bytes (null: the file must not exist); lock_after are the installed SKILL.md skill names.
offers: the first-run offer (no model): driven through offerModelAccess / offer_model_access with the answers mocked, a null answer being Ctrl+C or Ctrl+D at the question; printed as for cases.
